_readme: Season types per biome, for Serene Seasons in the overworld. Read by kubejs/data/creativecalendar/kubejs/sereneseasons/seasontags.js,
which fills the biome tags creativeworldgen:seasons/<type>; patcherMod seasons/SeasonTypes reads the tags.
Edit, then /reload (tags). Reference: feature_writeup/weather.md; per-biome result:
feature_writeup/weather_by_biome.md (python3 tools/gen_weather_table.py reads this file too).
arid       no rain or snow all year, temperature never changes, no seasonal grass tint, crops grow as in
summer all year. HUD: 'Arid', counting days through the year. Sand and terracotta biomes.
frozen     snow all year (temperature held at 0.1 or colder), nothing melts, no seasonal tint, only
winter crops. HUD: 'Frozen', counting days through the year.
dry        Serene Seasons' wet/dry cycle, rain in Mid Wet only (Late Winter + Early Spring), whatever the
biome declares. Savannas, shrublands and the other hot, dry grasslands.
tropical   Serene Seasons' wet/dry cycle, rain in every season but Mid Dry (Late Summer + Early Autumn).
Jungles, swamps, warm and lukewarm oceans.
temperate  Serene Seasons' temperate seasons (cools by up to 0.8 in winter), also above 0.8 where the mod
would make the biome tropical. Used for oceans and for temperate_highlands.
cold       temperate seasons (cools by up to 0.8 in winter), but snows exactly Late Autumn to Early Spring and
rains the rest of the year. Taiga, windswept, highland and cold-ocean biomes.
permanent_spring / permanent_summer / permanent_autumn / permanent_winter
one season all year (the Terralith skylands): no seasonal temperature, the HUD, grass tint and crops
show that season. Winter = frozen, shown as Winter. Summer never snows. Spring and autumn split the
year Early 1/4, Mid 1/2, Late 1/4 (HUD shows the part and its day); they snow only in their Early
Spring / Late Autumn, which falls in the world's winter, and rain the rest of the year.
adaptive   rivers and beaches: each column takes the type and temperature of the nearest land biome
(CEConfig [seasons] adaptiveRadius), so a river is arid in a desert and tropical in a jungle.
Any listed biome has seasons even if Serene Seasons' blacklist names it (the oceans are on it).
Oceans get seasonal weather (rain/snow) but only frozen-listed oceans freeze over; the rest keep vanilla ice (none).
A biome in none of the lists keeps Serene Seasons' own rule: tropical if it is in the server config's
tropical_biomes or warmer than 0.8, temperate otherwise; blacklisted biomes (caves) stay vanilla.
Only one list per biome; the order of precedence in code is arid, frozen, permanent_winter, permanent_spring,
permanent_summer, permanent_autumn, dry, tropical, cold, temperate.
snow_seasons: biome -> the sub-seasons it may snow in; any other sub-season it rains instead, however cold
Serene Seasons makes it. Names: early_spring ... late_winter, or a whole season (spring, summer, autumn,
winter). [] = never snows. Biomes not listed snow whenever they are cold enough. Frozen and permanent
biomes ignore it (their type decides). Applies below the snow line, CEConfig [seasons] snowLineY (320, build
height): below it height alone never turns rain into snow; at and above it temperate and cold biomes always
snow. Filled into the tags creativeworldgen:snow/no_<sub_season> by seasontags.js.
